target_customer: Developers and startups building web and mobile apps, increasingly including AI coding tools that provision databases
problem: Developers wanted the speed of Firebase on top of open standard Postgres without proprietary lock in.
business_model: hosted usage and tier based Postgres platform with an open source core
product_category: Postgres backend as a service and developer platform

founders.name: Paul Copplestone
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch give no background.

founders.name: Ant Wilson
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch give no background.

competitors.name: Google Firebase
competitors.what: Proprietary backend as a service with a NoSQL database, auth and realtime sync; the product Supabase's May 2020 launch explicitly positioned against

technical_complexity.rationale: Isolated Postgres per project with generated APIs, auth with row level security and realtime streams required deep Postgres and infrastructure skill, though built from existing open source parts.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and standard Postgres mean low lock in by design, so defensibility rests on developer mindshare, hosting scale and integrations rather than proprietary technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not eliminate it; Supabase grew to a reported 4 million developers and a 5 billion dollar valuation by October 2025.

market_need_then: A retrospective on the May 2020 Hacker News post says the open source Firebase alternative post drew over 1,120 upvotes and became the second most popular Launch HN, indicating strong developer demand for a Postgres based option.

branding.domain_note: The company site moved from supabase.io (docs path seen in a 2020 forum thread) to supabase.com; the date of the switch was not found.

identity.logo: Green lightning bolt symbol; primary Supabase green #3ECF8E per the official brand page
identity.visual_style: Dark theme with emerald green accent, developer focused
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and developer focused; tagline Build in a weekend. Scale to millions.

branding.brand_signature: The open source Firebase alternative positioning and the green bolt
branding.community_and_virality: May 2020 Hacker News post reached over 1,120 upvotes and a Product Hunt launch placed third of the day with 818 upvotes, per a Basedash retrospective; the company also runs recurring launch weeks.

brand_strength.rationale: The Firebase alternative positioning and developer community launches drove strong early awareness, and many third party design systems imitate its look. No source isolates the name itself as the driver.

outcome_analysis: Supabase launched an open source Firebase alternative on Hacker News in May 2020, raised a 6 million dollar seed in December 2020, and then stacked Series A through E rounds, reaching a reported 5 billion dollar valuation in October 2025 with 4 million developers. AI coding tools using it as the default database added a tailwind. A further 150 million dollar round and Turso acquisition were reported in October 2026.
notes: Series A and B exact months conflict: aggregators date Series A to September 2021 while Supabase's blog URL shows October 28, 2021, and press dates Series B to May 10, 2022 while the company write up is dated August 12, 2022; only years are recorded. The seed amount and investors come from an aggregator (startupintros) and a search summary; the Series A blog confirms Coatue led the seed. The Series C post money is a PitchBook estimate quoted by TechCrunch. CB Insights and Komo list the Series E as 120 million dollars versus the company's 100 million dollars; the company figure is used. The 2026 round and Turso acquisition come from a secondary outlet, not the company, and a reported 10.5 billion dollar valuation from a headline was not opened so it is not recorded. The competitor source is a retrospective, not a 2020 article; Nhost and Appwrite were also mentioned as rivals but without dated sources.
